676.canonical: Never treat a single item as evidence of mastery, since a student may respond correctly from a memorised answer or incorrectly because one item's idiosyncratic feature misled him: use multiple items and ask not how many are correct but whether that number dependably indicates mastery — convention suggests ten or twenty for an arithmetic rule, while sequential-analysis assumptions permit a decision on as few as three, with two of three correct giving confidence because two items can yield an uninterpretable half-right result.
